This is a list of people who have served as [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor") or president of the [city council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo_City_Council "Sarajevo City Council") of the city of [Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo "Sarajevo"), the capital of [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"). Sarajevo has had 40 different mayors in 41 different mayorships since the position was created on 22 August 1878, upon [Austro-Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary") [occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_campaign_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_in_1878 "Austro-Hungarian campaign in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1878").
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_mayors_of_Sarajevo&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
The first mayor of Sarajevo [Mustafa Fadilpašić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustafa_Fadilpa%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Mustafa Fadilpašić") was also the city's longest-served mayor, having remained in office for 14 years.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Sarajevo#cite_note-2) The first non-[Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") mayor was [Aristotel Petrović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aristotel_Petrovi%C4%87 "Aristotel Petrović"), who served from 1918 until 1920.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Sarajevo#cite_note-3) The only mayor to serve more than once was [Edhem Bičakčić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edhem_Bi%C4%8Dak%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Edhem Bičakčić"), who was mayor from 1928 to 1929, and once again from 1935 to 1939.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Sarajevo#cite_note-4) [Fehim Čurčić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fehim_%C4%8Cur%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Fehim Čurčić"), the city's fifth mayor, served during [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). In 1941, Atih Hadžikadić was elected mayor, a position that was short-lived as he was hanged during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") in August 1941. [Semiha Borovac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiha_Borovac "Semiha Borovac") became Sarajevo's first female mayor in 2005.
The current, 41st mayor of the city is [Samir Avdić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samir_Avdi%C4%87 "Samir Avdić"), serving since 16 July 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Sarajevo#cite_note-5)
